rationale.conceptual: The method uses standard DFT techniques but demands careful implementation of supercell geometries, defect formation enthalpies, antisite-based substitution schema, and ideal shear strength calculations. Multiple interacting components (formation energies, energy factors, correlative energies, stress-strain curves) require solid domain knowledge and attention to detail, placing it at a non-trivial level.
rationale.execution: The pipeline spans lattice optimization, supercell generation, multiple DFT relaxations for single and double defects, and shear deformation series (multiple strain steps per configuration). With ~10 load-bearing DFT jobs plus post-processing, robust file handling, and numerical analysis, the orchestration is lengthy and fragile.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires a series of DFT calculations on Ni3Al-Re supercells to reproduce site-preference energy, correlative energies, and ideal shear strengths. The method is established (DFT with plane-wave pseudopotentials) but involves careful supercell setup, force relaxation, and shear deformation simulations. The pipeline is long with many sequential DFT jobs, file management, and formula-based post-processing, making execution complex. Resources are modest, as supercells are small and can run on CPU.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small supercells (32–108 atoms) and low plane-wave cutoff (350 eV) allow execution on a single multi-core CPU; negligible input data.
